events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Muskegon by boat.** It has the best recent boat report (rated 3, good).
- **St. Joseph is a close second** (rated 3, good), if you'd rather run a shorter trip.
- **Fish deep:** start around 140 to 250 feet of water, with lines about 65 to 130 feet down.
- **Lures:** glow spoons, meat rigs, and green or white flies. Use the glow spoons in low light.
- **Skip South Haven** (rated 1, below average) unless you have no other choice.

Ratings for this week: Muskegon 3, St. Joseph 3, Grand Haven 2, South Haven 1.

## Why

- Muskegon's boat report was good: the Aug 3 Muskegon report rated boat fishing good, with fish 65 to 130 feet down in 140 to 250 feet of water.
- St. Joseph was also good: the Aug 3 St. Joseph report said meat rigs and spoons were catching most fish, in water well beyond 100 feet.
- South Haven was slow: the Aug 3 South Haven report called it "on the slow side," with the best water around 100 feet.
- I'd expect the deep, low-light bite to hold this week, since the Aug 3 reports at a similar water temperature said low light helped.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is Aug 3, six days old; no reports from the week of Aug 9)
- Muskegon (2022-08-03), boat, rated 3: "A mix of glow spoons, meat rigs, and green or white flies all worked well. The bite was good during low light conditions."
- St. Joseph (2022-08-03), boat, rated 3: "Salmon fishing was good… the fish moved in quite a bit. Both were well beyond 100 feet of water."
- Grand Haven (2022-08-03), boat, rated 2: "Boat anglers found the salmon action to be fair in 120 to 220 feet of water. The best bite was 65 to 140 down on green flies and meat rigs."
- South Haven (2022-08-03), boat, rated 1: "Salmon fishing was on the slow side but there were a few fish caught."
- Earlier July reports were weaker. Grand Haven and Muskegon were both rated 0 (slow) on 2022-07-14, and St. Joseph was rated 1 on 2022-07-20.

**Past seasons**
- The similar-temperature search (76 F ±3, within 14 days of today) returned only the same Aug 3 reports. It found no earlier-year matches, so I have no historical comparison for this water temperature.

**Conditions now**
- The buoy surface water for the week before Aug 9 averaged 76 F, up 1 F over the week, at all four ports (Muskegon and Grand Haven share buoy 45029; St. Joseph uses 45026; South Haven uses 45168). This is measured.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52 to 58 F. At 76 F at the surface, I'd expect the fish to sit deeper, in the cooler water below the thermocline.

## Caveats

- The newest report is from Aug 3, six days old. Conditions may have changed, and I have no reports from this week.
- Live conditions were unavailable. The tool returned a summary for the week before Aug 9, so I have no wind forecast and no modeled cold-layer depth. Check the forecast before you go, especially if winds are strong.
- The ratings for this week are my projection from the Aug 3 reports, not a report for this week.

## Sources

- Muskegon, Grand Haven, South Haven, St. Joseph (Aug 3 DNR bulletin): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3268d0b
- Grand Haven and Muskegon (July 14 DNR bulletin): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c
- St. Joseph (July 20 DNR bulletin): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/323f6bf
